answer: Each alias earns a renewal-decay reputation: its weight decays every epoch unless refreshed by verified paid work, so a sybil swarm loses standing the very dawn after it stops earning — velvet influence must be re-earned, never stockpiled. Spinning up n aliases costs registration plus n ongoing refresh fees to miners who verify close work, so cost(n) grows super-linearly for any coalition, not one operator; a spiral of cheap fresh IDs buys nothing, since unrefreshed weight decays to zero. Attackers must out-compete honest earners to matter.
